Key insights

Contract mix improving
Contracted revenue (In Contract + Annual) reached 52.3% in June — first month above month-to-month — up from 37.4% in January. M2M fell $260K to $188K.
RTM concentration risk
RTM is 94.0% of booked revenue ($2.583M of $2.747M). Unify360 ($124.9K) and NoDig ($38.8K) stay small; any RTM cancellation spike hits the total directly.
Cancellations peaked in June
Cancellations hit $58.1K in June, the highest month ($169.3K YTD). SEO and LSA drove most of it.
Active clients declining
Active clients fell from 246 (Jan) to 210 (Jul MTD). June recovered to 230 before July resumed the slide.
Net recurring deficit
New recurring ($87.4K YTD) trails cancellations ($169.3K) by −$81.9K — every month except April ran a deficit.
Revenue holding near $400K/mo
Monthly booked held $388–416K through June (avg $399.0K); July is $364K MTD and firms up as billing completes.

Key insights

July is mid-month
40.5% of July's $372,025 booked has been collected so far, against 98.6% for June at close. Mid-month, not a collection problem — the figure to watch is the $216,748 still outstanding.
RTM concentration risk
RTM is 94.0% of booked revenue ($2.583M of $2.747M). Any acceleration in cancellations hits the total directly.
Recurring runs a deficit
New sales ($270.9K YTD) beat cancellations ($169.3K) by +$101.6K, but on recurring alone it's a −$81.9K deficit ($87.4K new recurring vs $169.3K cancelled).
Expansion softens but doesn't cover churn
Upgrades beat downgrades by +$33.6K YTD (existing accounts are growing), but that only partly offsets the −$81.9K recurring deficit — the recurring base is still net −$47.9K for the year.
Cancellations peaked in June
Cancellations hit $58.1K in June, the highest month; $169.3K YTD across all entities.
Active clients declining
Active clients fell from 246 (Jan) to 210 (Jul MTD) — 14.6%, the clearest attrition signal.
Concentration to watch
SEO + LSA drive 45% of service revenue ($1.05M); Unify360 ($124.9K) and NoDig ($38.8K) stay small but steady.
Collection is healthy
91.8% of booked revenue is collected ($2.538M paid YTD); $227.9K outstanding — mostly July recurring, which clears as the month closes.

Key insights

Madison leads profitability
Madison nets $449.5K with a 91.4% win ratio — 64 recurring campaigns and only 6 cancellations.
Veronica carries the most attrition
24 cancellations ($42.4K) and the lowest win ratio (54.7%) — the clearest AM-level retention risk.
SEO is the service anchor
SEO is the largest recurring service ($678.0K) yet holds a low 6.3% attrition rate — the stable core of the book.
LSA is the attrition watch-item
LSA has the highest attrition (9.6%, $39.3K lost) and churns in both directions (top upgrades & downgrades) — nets positive but needs monitoring.
Upgrades outpace downgrades
+$33.8K net YTD ($77.3K upgrades vs $43.5K downgrades) — expansion is outrunning contraction.
Blended attrition stays healthy
6.8% blended attrition across services; most sit under 8%, and RTM Package & Design show 0% churn YTD.

Key insights

Forecast trending down
Recurring forecast fell from $296.7K (Feb) to $231.9K (Jul) — a ~22% decline as cumulative churn outpaces retention.
RTM drives the decline
RTM forecast dropped $272.4K to $213.3K, while Unify360 and NoDig held near flat — the decline is concentrated in RTM.
June churn hit hardest
June's $58.1K cancellation spike is the single largest drag, pulling the July forecast down the most of any month.
Completed sales is the biggest deduction
One-time completed sales (non-recurring) are the largest monthly deduction — e.g. −$66.5K in the June→July step.
Forecast is a conservative floor
The model runs below actual recurring each month — it deducts all churn but adds no new recurring wins, so treat it as a floor, not a midpoint.
Small entities stay stable
Unify360 (~$14–20K) and NoDig (~$4–5K) hold steady across every month — low volatility, reliable base.

Paid base declining

Outstanding improved in June

Key insights

Sales declining year over year
Total sales fell $6.51M (2023) → $5.89M (2025); 2026 YTD ($2.74M) tracks ~21% below 2025’s Jan–Jul pace.
GBP is the sharpest decline
GBP collapsed −59% ($1.63M → $673K, 2023→2025) — the single biggest drag on the service mix.
SEO remains the anchor
SEO is the #1 service every year and still the largest revenue driver — the stable core despite market softness.
Cancellations accelerating
2026 YTD cancellations ($169.3K) are +63% vs 2025 YTD ($103.8K) — the clearest risk signal in the book.
Attrition mix has shifted
The top cancellation service moved from GBP (2023–24) to SEO (2025–26) — churn now follows the largest service.
New sales more resilient
New sales fell ~20.5% YTD vs 2025 ($270.9K vs $289.0K prorated) — contraction is broad, not just recurring.

Annual summary — all years

EntityMetric20222023202420252026 YTDTrend
Formula: EBITDA = (Sales − Operational Expense) + Interest + Taxes (Payroll) + Depreciation + Amortization Sources: QuickBooks P&L (authoritative). Interest = QB "Interest Paid" (RTM) / "Interest Expense" (U360). D&A = $0 (not recorded in QB for either entity). Dec figures (FY2022–2025) include QB year-end payroll tax true-up adjustments.

Key insights

RTM FY2023 was peak performance
$6.16M revenue and $2.52M EBITDA at 40.9% margin — the strongest year on record. The business demonstrated it can sustain 40%+ margins at scale.
FY2024–25 margin compression
RTM margins dropped to 30.5% (FY24) and 29.0% (FY25) due to cost growth outpacing revenue. FY2026 YTD is recovering strongly back to 38.9%.
U360 is recovering
U360 EBITDA improved from -$936K (FY23) → -$776K (FY24) → -$216K (FY25) → near breakeven in FY26 YTD. The loss trajectory is clearly reversing.
Combined story is positive
Combined EBITDA of ~$877K YTD Jan–Jul 2026 at 36.6% margin — annualizes to ~$1.75M, recovering toward the FY22–23 levels.
Dec true-ups distort monthly view
December figures each year include large payroll tax year-end adjustments. Use annual totals for trend analysis, not individual months.
D&A = $0 across all years
Neither RTM nor U360 records Depreciation or Amortization in QuickBooks. If a separate depreciation schedule exists, those figures can be added as ITDA components.

Key insights

OpEx down 16.1% Jan–Jun
Total operating expense fell from $216.8K (Jan) to $181.9K (Jun) — $1.204M YTD. Five consecutive months of decline before June.
Payroll is 79.9% of OpEx
At $962.7K of $1.204M YTD, payroll dominates the cost base. Card charges ($144.2K) are a distant second at 12.0%.
May's drop was card-driven, not payroll
The $25.0K May decline came 53% from card charges (−$13.3K, 43% below their 6-month average) and only 30% from payroll. June reversed it: card charges rebounded $10.0K, the first month-over-month OpEx increase (+$3.1K).
Payroll declining 15.6% Jan–Jun
Total payroll dropped from $171.7K (Jan) to $144.9K (Jun) — $962.7K YTD.
Executive = largest dept cost
At $32.6K/mo, executive overhead is the single largest department cost — 24.9% of the $131.1K monthly total.
PH payroll = 66.7% of total
PH team at $641.8K YTD (70 staff) vs. US at $320.9K (5 staff) — 2.0× the US spend. On June payroll over the current 75-person roster that is $1,433/mo per PH head vs. $8,914/mo per US head, a 6.2× unit-cost gap.
